note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of 00d8bf62b7). RFC 6286 Section 2.1: "The BGP Identifier is a 4-octet, unsigned, non-zero integer that should be unique within an AS. The value of the BGP Identifier for a BGP speaker is determined on startup and is the same for every local interface and every BGP peer." 00d8bf62b7 widened the {partial} Gap to "is determined on startup and is the same for every local interface and every BGP peer" and names the second Producer, internal/component/bgp/reactor/reload_globals.go::applyGlobalsJournaled. Read at HEAD: applyGlobalsJournaled records r.setGlobals(globals) whenever the reloaded Globals differ, so a reload replaces the global RouterID while the daemon runs and the peer diff restarts every peer whose effective identifier changed (TestReloadAppliesGlobalRouterID, green); the startup clause is therefore unmet, and the annotation's Gap now matches the Support remaining disclosure, which closes the finding carried from 2026-10-21. parsePeerSettings still lets a peer or group override the global with session router-id (peer-level overrides global), the owner-approved deviation (Q2, 2026-10-13), not counted conformant. Tested 'non-zero integer' stands: parseRouterID returns an error for 0.0.0.0 on both the global leaf (GlobalsFromTree) and the per-peer override; TestParsePeerFromTreeInvalid zero_router_id_rejected and TestRFC6286GlobalZeroRouterIDRejected assert the exact RFC 6286 Section 2.1 error, and TestRFC6286NonZeroRouterIDAccepted plus the 0.0.0.1 half of the global test assert identifier 1 is accepted, so removing or widening the zero check turns them red; all ran green at HEAD under -race. Observation: the tag polarity words read opposite to the skill's wording (positive tags the rejecting cases, negative the accepting ones); both directions are present with exact assertions, so the pair holds. Partial, zero whole-requirement credit.
